findings.visibleEvidence: The reviewed classic-hub ARIA tree contains one main landmark wrapping the page and a second main landmark nested inside it immediately before the ten game cards. The visual catalog has a clear single-page hierarchy, so the second nested landmark does not represent a distinct document main region.
findings.whyItMatters: Screen-reader landmark navigation can announce two visible main regions with one nested inside the other, making the otherwise clear catalog hierarchy less predictable and forcing assistive-technology users to infer which main region is authoritative.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the outer page main landmark and change the inner game-card container to a non-main section or div with an appropriate accessible label if one is useful; then review and re-establish the classic-hub ARIA snapshot without changing its visible card layout.

findings.visibleEvidence: The forest camp screenshot has a persistent visual title, '汉字魔法战 · 墨迹森林', but the reviewed camp ARIA tree exposes it only as plain text and contains no heading. When overlays open, their names begin at heading level 2, so the route's accessible heading hierarchy has no level-1 page anchor.
findings.whyItMatters: Users who navigate by headings cannot identify or return to the game route's primary heading, and level-2 overlay headings have no exposed level-1 parent even though the visual hierarchy clearly supplies one.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose the existing persistent visual game title as the route's single level-1 heading without changing its appearance, and retain named overlay/dialog headings at level 2; re-review the camp, ability-choice, and spellbook ARIA snapshots afterward.

findings.visibleEvidence: At 320px width the export button's full technical filename wraps across several lines and splits the TEST and OBSERVATION tokens mid-word. The ARIA evidence preserves the full accessible name and the deep-route/scroll evidence records zero horizontal overflow, so this is a scanability defect rather than lost functionality.
findings.whyItMatters: The adult observer remains operable, but the most important final action is slower to recognize on the narrow supported viewport because its label is dominated by a broken technical filename.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a short visible action label such as '导出观察 JSON' while preserving the exact generated filename in the download attribute and, if needed, an adjacent description; keep the existing full accessible context and target size.

limitations: This review is based on deterministic screenshots, ARIA snapshots, scroll/deep-route records, and synthetic agent playthroughs; it does not prove real-child comfort, preference, understanding, or sustained engagement.

Static evidence cannot prove subjective motion comfort or the behavior of every browser and assistive-technology combination; reduced-motion availability and tested state coverage are machine evidence only.
The PRE_CHANGE_REFERENCE is reference-only and was used to check continuity of existing child surfaces; it is not treated as prior visual or accessibility acceptance.
